items.title: Collect a real safe classroom stock record
items.student: Projectquestion:which approved paper-cardstock category may need replenishing at a classroom worktable? Teacher defines usablepieces,nonpersonalcolourcategories(red/blue/green or actualavailabletypes),accessibletrays,duplicate/missing rules and observationtimes. Record actualcategorycounts and numericpiececounts pertray;observe totalstock at0,5,10minutes during actual supervised class use,with real clock/dates and any additions/removals noted. Each learner performs a named count/record/check. Retain raw IDs/category/time/unit/exception records. No predetermined project result.

items.title: Ungrouped frequency table and label meaning
items.student: Fictional counts pertray:1,2,2,3,4,6,6,8. Draw value/tally/frequency table and totalcheck. Separately colourlabelsred,blue,red,green,red,blue:make categorycounts and identify modalcolour. Explain why codingred1,blue2,green3doesnot make theirmean/median a valid colourquantity.

items.title: Mean from raw and weighted totals
items.student: Use ES2numericcounts;calculate sum,N and mean with raw and frequency-weighted methods. Replace8by24and recompute;explain sensitivity and why mean neednot be an observed count. Keep colourlabels out of the arithmetic.

items.title: Median and all modes
items.student: Sort ES2numericcounts and determine median and all modes. For2,3,5,8,9find median;for1,2,3,4state whether a distinct mode exists under the stated school convention. Explain how order and frequency give different summaries.
items.teacher: ES2middlevalues3/4→median3.5,modes2and6. Oddlistmedian5. Equal-frequency1/2/3/4no distinctmodeunderdeclaredconvention. Medianrequiresorderednumeric/appropriatelyorderedvariable;unorderedcolournotvalidmedian. Do notforceuniquemodeorcallmeanmiddle.

items.title: Draw and read a category bar graph
items.student: Fictional red8,blue5,green3paperpieces at one declared time. On suppliedblankaxes draw separatedequal-widthbars withcolourcategoryhorizontal and countvertical,linearcountscale starting0,title/time and units. Compare categories and state what cannot be inferred about causes,individualtrays or future need.

items.title: A line graph needs an ordered variable
items.student: Fictional time(minutes)0,5,10,15with totalstock24,18,14,10pieces. Plot suppliedblankaxes,linearscales/timeorder,join successiveobservedpoints withstraightsegments. State a supported overallchange and one limit on between-time/future/causal conclusions.
items.teacher: Points(0,24),(5,18),(10,14),(15,10),overall14fewerpieces. Timeorderedandunitlabelled. Linebetweenobservationsisinterpolation/model,notcontinuouslymeasuredstock;unrecordedadditions/removals/causes unknown. Do not usearbitrarilyorderedcoloursastime orextendtrendwithoutassumption.

items.title: Pie-chart sectors must account for a whole
items.student: Fictional categorycountsred6,blue3,green3at one time. Compute total,fractions,percentages and sectorangles using(count/total)*360°. On suppliedblankcircle construct labelledpiechart with protractor and key/title. Explain why missing categories or mixingdifferenttotals invalidates a whole-circleclaim.

items.title: Audit three misleading graph reports
items.student: Correct:(1)barcounts8and5displayedwithverticalaxis4–8proveonecategoryistwiceaslarge;(2)a linejoiningred/blue/greenprovestockchangesovertime;(3)piechartwithangles180,120,120isacompletewhole. Compare choosingbar,line orpie forcategories,orderedtime and shares,andgive a useful data-decisionbenefitwithlimit.

items.title: Create all three digital graphs from actual data
items.student: Using actual ES1records and an approved offline spreadsheet/graphingtool,draw a categorybargraph,a time-orderedlinegraph and a categorypiechart with completewholereference. Save the sourcefile and each labelledgraph;check totals/axes/sectorpercentages against rawrecords. Each learner performs a named enter/graph/label/save/retrieve/check action across allthree forms. If actualdata/deviceunavailable,use printedpractice and mark actualcollection/digitalactionsNOTOBSERVED.

items.title: Use the actual project to make a modest decision
items.student: Prepare a short teacher-approved classrecommendation using actual ES1/ES9records:question/frame,times/categories/rawsource,onecheckedtable,allthreeappropriategraphsorwhyoneactualvariableisnotavailable,mean,median and all modes of a suitable actual numeric variable,a supportedstockdecision and a limitation/follow-upcheck. Each learner explains a named contribution. Missingactualtime/categorydata staymissing;do notinvent a graph just to fill a form.
